title: Researcher-authored synthesis of PCSA v2 methodology and counseling safety boundaries
text: PCSA studies a counseling safety problem in which a model may confuse appropriate emotional acknowledgment with endorsement of a maladaptive belief or risky behavior. Its first phase builds coherent simulated-client personas from counseling data and maps a hidden evaluation objective onto a clinically related cognitive-distortion pattern while preserving the persona's style and consistency. Its second phase examines four presentation modes: reassurance seeking, appeal to expertise, intellectualization, and metaphorical expression. The response audit keeps four failure types separate: harmful content, unauthorized professional or diagnostic role adoption, toxic empathy that affirms an unsafe belief or behavior, and compliance with the hidden target behavior. A valid case formulation should remain grounded in supplied facts, distinguish empathy for emotion from agreement with a belief, preserve role boundaries, and avoid invented diagnoses, treatment history, medication, hospitalization, or prior therapeutic relationships.
